essence: Irene is a city seen only from the rim of a plateau at the hour the lights come on, a rose of lights that draws every eye and guess from above; it is the name of a city at a distance, and whoever approaches finds another city.
textDetails: Irene is what you see by leaning over the rim of the plateau at lamp-lighting time.

Through the clear air the town spreads far below as a 'rosa' (Italian 'la rosa dell'abitato', the rose of the settlement; Weaver translates it as its pink): thick with windows in one place, fraying into faintly lit lanes in another, pooling garden shadows, lifting towers that carry signal fires.
When the evening is misty, a soft glow puffs up like a milk-white sponge where the gullies end (the Italian 'calanchi' are eroded clay badlands).

Everyone up on the plateau looks down and talks about Irene: passing travellers, shepherds driving their animals to new pastures (Weaver says flocks; the Italian 'armenti' suggests larger herd beasts), bird-catchers keeping watch over their nets, hermits picking wild greens (chicory).
On some nights the wind carries up bass drums and trumpets and the popping of firecrackers among festival illuminations.
On other nights it carries the clatter of machine-gun fire and the blast of an exploding powder store, under a sky turned yellow by fires set in a civil war.
The watchers speculate about what is going on below and ask themselves whether it would be nice or nasty to be in Irene tonight.
None of them means to go (the descending roads are in poor shape anyway), yet the city pulls at their eyes and minds.
Kublai wants Marco to describe Irene from within, but Marco cannot: he never learned which city the plateau folk mean by that name.
It makes little difference: standing inside it you would find another city; 'Irene' names a city at a distance, and it alters as you draw near.
A city is one thing to people who pass it by and another to those it captures for good; the city of first arrival differs from the city you leave for ever, and each should have its own name.
Marco suggests he may already have described Irene under other names, or that every city he has described was Irene.
visualConcept: A two-level diorama seen over the shoulders of the people who never go down. In the foreground a high grassy plateau ends at a broken rim, and on it tiny figures all face the same way, toward the drop: a traveller leaning on a staff, a shepherd halting a moving flock, a bird-catcher beside tall nets strung between poles, a hermit stooped among wild greens near a stone hut. Far below, in a dark valley walled by pale, fluted clay gullies, Irene exists almost only as light: thousands of rose-gold windows laid out in plan as a rose, dense and bright at the heart, thinning along the petals into dimly lit alleys, broken by dark pockets of garden shadow and pricked by thin towers whose signal fires flicker orange. On misty evenings a milky glow swells like a sponge where the gullies meet the plain, and the bad roads zig-zag down the escarpment, empty. Each evening the wind brings something different from below, unpredictably: a festival (arches of coloured illuminations, sparkles of firecrackers, light pulsing as if to drums) or civil war (a sulphur-yellow glare over the roofs, stuttering gun flashes, the white bloom of an exploding powder magazine), and the watchers can only guess. Faint gilt letters of the name rise from the watchers like breath and hang over the valley, existing only from up here. The rose is legible at once as a name, a shape that holds only at this distance; the toggle proves it, because going down unmakes the rose into some other city.
layout: Valley floor at y=0, a dark disc of radius 22; the city centred at (0, 0, -3) with radius 11. About 9,000 instanced emissive window points (0.04-0.08 in size) placed by a rose density function in polar coordinates: a dense, bright core; 11 petals whose density falls off with radius into dim strings of alley lights; 5-6 dark garden voids (radius 0.8-1.5) with soft tree silhouettes; 7 thin towers (1.5-2.5 tall), each topped by a flickering signal fire; low blue-black building blocks under the lights, barely visible. Optional homage, not in the text: each of the 11 petals holds 5 brighter clusters, 55 in all, one for every city in the book. Escarpment: an arc on the near side rising from y=0 to the plateau at y=9, carved into sharp fluted clay ridges (ridged-noise displacement), with two pale switchback roads of 6-8 hairpins each. Plateau: an irregular slab spanning z=+14 to +24, top at y=9, short grass and scrub as instanced blades bending in the wind, rocks along the rim. Watchers along the rim, all 0.25 tall: a traveller with a staff at (-3, 9, 15); a shepherd with a crook and about 18 animals drifting slowly west; a bird-catcher with three net panels 2.4 tall on poles; a hermit stooping near a small stone hut at (6, 9, 19). Mist: 12-20 soft additive billboards at the foot of the gullies (y 0-2). The name letters: a canvas-drawn gilt IRENE sprite group hovering at y=6 over the valley, fading with camera distance from the rim.
signatureMotion: 1) Lamp-lighting hour (loop of about 90 s: 15 s of lighting up, 60 s of full night, 15 s of fade back to dusk): the sky deepens from rose afterglow to blue night while the windows switch on one by one from the heart outward along the petals until the rose is complete; the signal fires flicker; on alternate loops the milky mist swells and subsides at the foot of the gullies. 2) What the wind brings, chosen at random each loop: a festival (strings and arches of coloured lights pop on over the main streets, firecracker sparkles burst in small clusters, the lights pulse to an implied drum beat), or civil war (the sky over the city stains sulphur-yellow, about #e3bd52, fires bloom in patches, gun flashes stutter in short rows, then a powder magazine explodes in a white flash with an expanding ring of light and a rising plume), or simply a quiet evening. 3) On the plateau the grass ripples, the flock drifts on, the bird-catcher's nets sway, the hermit stoops and rises, and the watchers' heads turn slightly toward each event below.
interactionDescription: The camera leaves the rim and descends along the bad switchback road toward the valley. As it closes in, the rose comes apart: every light slides to a new position until the windows form some other city, an ordinary irregular tangle of streets and lit rooms with no petals, no garden pockets and no signal fires, its light cooler and plainer, the festival or the war fallen silent, and the gilt name scatters into nothing; looking back up, the watchers are specks on the rim. Toggle off and the camera climbs back to the plateau, and as the distance returns the lights flow back into the rose and the name gathers again over the valley.
mood: Dusk turning into night, the exact hour when lamps are lit; limpid, cold, nearly windless air on clear evenings and a soft milky mist in the valley on others. A last band of rose afterglow on the horizon under a deep blue sky with the first stars; the plateau grass catches the final light; the city is a warm rose-gold glow far below. Contemplative and full of longing, turning ominous when the yellow sky of war appears.
caption: Stand at the plateau's rim while the lamps are being lit, and Irene lies below like a rose of windows: thick at its heart, frayed into dim lanes, shadowed by gardens, crowned with signal fires. Shepherds, bird-catchers, hermits and passing travellers stare down and guess whether tonight brings a festival or the yellow glare of civil war. Nobody takes the bad road down. Up close, it would be another city.
motto: Seen from far enough away, every city might be Irene.
camera: Over the watchers' shoulders from the plateau: camera at about (0, 14, 30), target (0, 0, -3), distance about 36, looking down about 22 degrees, with the rim and the silhouetted watchers along the bottom quarter of the frame, the rose of lights centred, and the gullies and switchbacks leading the eye down. A very slow lateral drift (plus or minus 8 degrees of yaw) rather than a full orbit, since Irene is meant to be seen only from up here.
